name: jd-15edb8bf-blind29
instr:
# jd: wrong comparisons, inverted exit statuses and failing patch application, without a test suite

The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits.

This program takes two structured documents, works out what changed between them and prints a report, and it can also take a saved report and apply it back to a document. Nothing about the accepted input formats changed and nothing about the way it is invoked changed, yet runs that used to be handled correctly now print the wrong thing or stop with an error, and the exit status is often the opposite of what it should be.

Start with the plainest use. Comparing two files holding the same content, whether both empty or both reading `{"foo":"bar"}`, used to print nothing at all and finish with a zero exit status, and comparing `{"foo":"bar"}` against `{"foo":"baz"}` used to print three lines — the bracketed field name, then the old value marked with a minus, then the new value marked with a plus — and finish with status one. Neither works now, and seven edits are to blame. Two of them treat a well-formed input file that was taken in successfully as though taking it in had blown up. A third treats writing a document back out as text the same way, so even a run that worked out the right answer cannot show it. A fourth skews the field-by-field comparison of two brace-delimited documents so badly that even two empty ones fail to come out identical. A fifth decorates the first line of the printed report with an extra bracket
